name: US immigration rules apply in Puerto Rico
summary: Puerto Rico is a US territory, so entry, visas, green cards and citizenship follow federal US law. There is no separate Puerto Rico visa. Act 60 is a local tax incentive program, not a visa or residency route.

other: Check travel.state.gov, uscis.gov and cbp.gov for the exact route. Act 60 grants no immigration status.

name: Visa Waiver Program (ESTA)
summary: Citizens of eligible countries can visit the US for business or tourism up to 90 days without a visa, after applying through ESTA. CBP officers decide admission on arrival.

other: CBP page does not name Puerto Rico, but it is US territory. Confirm eligible countries on the CBP list.

name: US Visitor Visa (B-1/B-2)
summary: Travelers from countries not in the Visa Waiver Program generally need a US visa in their passport. The type depends on the purpose of the trip.

other: Use the Visa Wizard on travel.state.gov to pick the right type.

name: US Naturalization
summary: Green card holders can become US citizens by meeting requirements set by Congress in the Immigration and Nationality Act. Citizenship can also pass from US citizen parents.

other: Years of residence, tests and dual citizenship rules not confirmed on a page I could open.
